question.text: Will Loudoun County pause final approvals for new Data Centers and Substations before December 16, 2026?
question.resolution_criteria: This question resolves as **Yes** if, before December 16, 2026, the Loudoun County Board of Supervisors formally adopts a resolution or other official Board action establishing a general pause on the Board's final votes on legislative applications for both data centers and electrical substations.
question.fine_print:
A generally applicable pause may contain exceptions, including for grid reliability or statutory decision deadlines, and still count.

The primary resolution sources will be official records of the [Loudoun](https://www.loudoun.gov/meetings) [County](https://www.loudoun.gov/m/newsflash/Home/Detail/10938) [Board of Supervisors](https://www.loudoun.gov/m/newsflash/home/detail/10874).

***
This question's information (resolution criteria, fine print, background info, etc) is synced with an [original identical question](https://www.metaculus.com/questions/46271) which opened on 2026-11-02 18:00:00. This question will resolve based on the resolution criteria and fine print of the linked original question. However, if this question would resolve differently than the original question, then this question will be annulled. Additionally, if the original question's resolution could have been known before this question opened, then this question will be annulled.

research:
I found nothing showing the pause has been adopted. As of 2026-11-07 the final Board vote is still set for **November 17, 2026**. Randall has postponed it twice, but a 7-member majority backed advancing it, and if the vote slips again there is likely at least one more Board meeting before December 16.

## 1. Resolution source
- 2026-10-20 (county news item 10938): the Board moved Agenda Item 14p, the resolution pausing its consideration of data center and substation applications, from October 20 to November 17 because "staff need more time." [loudoun.gov](https://www.loudoun.gov/m/newsflash/Home/Detail/10938)
- Undated county news item 10874, written before October 20: the pause would last up to 12 months, counted from each application's first Planning Commission hearing. The Board wants it to apply back to September 15. Exceptions could be made for grid reliability or when a statutory deadline is about to expire. Applications would not become inactive. [loudoun.gov](https://www.loudoun.gov/m/newsflash/home/detail/10874)
- The county also has a PDF titled "Statement - Loudoun Board Enacts Pause on Data Centers," with file metadata dated 2026-09-16. I could not read its text. Since the September vote only ordered a draft, this is probably a supervisor's statement and not an enactment, but I have not confirmed that. [loudoun.gov PDF](https://www.loudoun.gov/DocumentCenter/View/222331/Statement---Loudoun-Board-Enacts-Pause-on-Data-Centers)
- I did not check the official minutes or agenda at loudoun.gov/meetings. The November 17 agenda is normally posted at least three days before the meeting.

## 2. Current status
- Not settled. The pause has not been adopted and the final vote is set for 2026-11-17 at 4:00 p.m. [United Loudoun](https://unitedloudoun.org/issues/pause)
- 2026-09-15: the Board voted 7-1-0-1 to have staff draft the resolution. In a second 7-1-0-1 vote, it agreed the Board could still act during the pause on grid-reliability substations or applications near their statutory deadline. Those exceptions are allowed under the fine print. [United Loudoun](https://unitedloudoun.org/issues/pause), [mgrid](https://mgrid.org/2026/09/16/loudoun-county-voted-7-1-1-to-draft-a-data-center-pause-not-to-start-one/)

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-11-06: Supervisor Briskman gave warnings about the data center boom in an interview about Alberta. The article does not give a new pause date. [CP24](https://www.cp24.com/news/canada/2026/11/06/this-us-county-has-more-than-200-data-centres-heres-the-advice-it-has-for-alberta/)
- 2026-10-24: On October 20, Randall announced a deal under which Amazon drops its data center plan for the former GWU campus and gives up legal action over it. The report says most supervisors back the pause. [Yahoo Finance](https://finance.yahoo.com/real-estate/articles/amazon-just-walked-away-427-131246217.html)
- Late October 2026 (article undated): Chair Randall postponed the vote twice. Briskman objected, noting the Board had twice voted overwhelmingly to advance it, and asked "What changed?" [Blue Ridge Leader](https://blueridgeleader.com/supervisors-table-data-center-audit-as-pause-faces-delays/)
- 2026-10-20: Randall said the county attorney asked for the deferral after the county received requests from attorneys. She called it "just kind of a check and double-check" and said deferrals are generally allowed on a first request. [Loudoun Times-Mirror](https://www.loudountimes.com/news/business_and_economy/real_estate_and_development/county-board-defers-vote-on-data-center-pause/article_95602019-bdda-474f-819a-16d3d64645bf.html), [WJLA](https://wjla.com/news/local/loudoun-county-pushes-back-discussion-on-proposed-data-center-pause-virginia-electric-technology-ai)
- 2026-10-05: The Data Center Coalition and the Chamber of Commerce oppose the pause. Community groups and attorney Bryan Turner support it. Staff estimated $45M-60M in possible lawsuit costs, but that estimate is for ending grandfathering protections, a separate measure, not the pause. [Loudoun Now](https://www.loudounnow.com/news/loudoun-board-prepares-for-big-data-center-changes-as-lawsuit-threats-loom/article_b754549e-7bac-48b1-8f23-238b83fa0a2f.html)
- I found no lawsuit filed over the pause. One tracker said none had been filed as of September 16. [suedatacenters.org](https://suedatacenters.org/lawsuits/loudoun-county-data-center-pause-grandfathering)

## 4. Base rates
- 2022 to May 2026: the Board approved 32 of 39 legislative data center applications, so it has historically favored development (from the question background).
- 2026-09-15: the Board denied the Tech Park at Dulles substation 6-3, which suggests the current majority is skeptical. [United Loudoun](https://unitedloudoun.org/issues/pause)
- Similar places: Carroll County, MD adopted a one-year pause in February 2026 and extended it to 2028 on November 5. [Fox Baltimore](https://foxbaltimore.com/news/local/carroll-county-board-of-commissioners-extends-data-center-development-pause-through-2028-maryland)
- When a Board majority has voted to direct staff to draft a resolution, it usually passes in some form. The open risk is further deferral or watering-down. I found no hard numbers on this.

## 5. Other forecasts
- I found no Polymarket, Kalshi or Manifold market on the Loudoun pause.
- The Kalshi markets provided do not match this question: whether any state enacts a moratorium law before 2027 (0.29), before July 2027 (0.63), and before 2028 (0.94), plus Loudoun Water use. They only show the general climate.
- I could not get a Metaculus community forecast for question 46271.

## 6. Upcoming events before December 16
- 2026-11-17, 4:00 p.m.: Board business meeting with the scheduled final vote. The agenda should be posted around November 13-14. [United Loudoun](https://unitedloudoun.org/issues/pause)
- If it is deferred again, the Board's usual first-and-third-Tuesday schedule points to meetings around December 1 and December 15, both before the deadline. I have not confirmed the December calendar.
- Risks: legal review following requests from developer attorneys, the Chair's earlier postponements, and possible changes to the resolution's scope. Under the criteria it must still cover both data centers and substations.

Yes prices: Above 250 million gallons: 0.48; Above 300 million gallons: 0.20; Above 200 million gallons: 0.81; Above 350 million gallons: 0.10; Above 150 million gallons: 0.91; Above 450 million gallons: 0.04; Above 400 million gallons: 0.05.

- Kalshi: Which states will enact data center moratoriums before 2028? (Before Jan 1, 2028). Yes prices: Michigan: 0.49; Georgia: 0.47; New Hampshire: 0.58; Maine: 0.65; California: 0.29; Wisconsin: 0.32; Maryland: 0.30; New Mexico: 0.70; Indiana: 0.28; North Carolina: 0.27.
- Kalshi: Which data center ballot measures will pass? (In 2026). Yes prices: Joliet Township, Illinois advisory question: 0.05; Ashville, Ohio EdgeConneX referendum: 0.06; Boulder City, Nevada Question 1: 0.06; Alhambra, California Measure DB: 0.95; Trenton, Ohio Issue 17: 0.96; El Dorado, Kansas data center ordinance: 0.95; Emporia, Kansas Question 2: 0.97; Grove City, Ohio Issue 28: 0.97; Janesville, Wisconsin GM/JATCO referendum: 0.97; Piqua, Ohio Section 138 amendment: 0.97.

As of November 7, 2026, nothing settles this question yet. The Board has not adopted the pause. The resolution is scheduled for a vote on **November 17, 2026**, after one postponement, and the Board voted 7-1-1 in September to have staff draft it. I found no reporting from November 1 to 7 on the agenda packet or on how supervisors now lean.

### 1. Resolution source
- 2026-10-20: The county's news release (item 10938) says agenda item 14p, "Resolution to Pause Board of Supervisors Consideration of Legislative Applications for Data Centers and Substations," was moved from the October 20 meeting to **November 17**, because "staff need more time to develop information." The release does not record an adoption. [loudoun.gov](https://www.loudoun.gov/m/newsflash/Home/Detail/10938)
- Earlier release (item 10874): the pause would last up to 12 months and take effect retroactively to September 15. It would cover only final Board votes. Applications could still be filed and go through the Planning Commission. It would allow exceptions for grid reliability and for applications near their statutory deadline, and administrative applications are not affected. [loudoun.gov](https://www.loudoun.gov/m/newsflash/home/detail/10874)
- The meetings page sends readers to the eScribe calendar. Agenda packets usually go up the Thursday before a meeting, so about November 12 for the November 17 meeting. [loudoun.gov/meetings](https://www.loudoun.gov/meetings)
- A county PDF is titled "Statement - Loudoun Board Enacts Pause on Data Centers," but its file metadata dates it to September 16. It most likely covers the September directive vote, not an adoption. [loudoun.gov PDF](https://www.loudoun.gov/DocumentCenter/View/222331/Statement---Loudoun-Board-Enacts-Pause-on-Data-Centers)

### 2. Current status
- Not resolved. No resolution has been adopted, and the November 17 meeting has not happened yet.

### 3. Recent news (newest first)

- 2026-10-28: Blue Ridge Leader reports that Chair Randall has postponed the pause twice, first to October 20 and then to November 17. Briskman criticized the delay and asked for a public explanation, saying "Decisions of this importance should not be made behind closed doors." On October 6 the Board tabled TeKrony's $200K data center audit by 7-2, with Letourneau, Kershner, Umstattd, Turner and Randall raising objections. [Blue Ridge Leader](https://blueridgeleader.com/supervisors-table-data-center-audit-as-pause-faces-delays/)
- 2026-10-20: Randall said the County Attorney asked for the deferral to have more time to consult other attorneys. She said she grants a first deferral request as a matter of course. [Loudoun Times-Mirror](https://www.loudountimes.com/news/business_and_economy/real_estate_and_development/county-board-defers-vote-on-data-center-pause/article_95602019-bdda-474f-819a-16d3d64645bf.html); [WJLA](https://wjla.com/news/local/loudoun-county-pushes-back-discussion-on-proposed-data-center-pause-virginia-electric-technology-ai)
- 2026-09-15: The Board voted 7-1-1 to direct staff to draft the pause resolution. Umstattd voted no and Kershner abstained. A second 7-1-1 vote, with Briskman opposed, added the grid-reliability exception. Letourneau questioned whether substations should be included. County Attorney Leo Rogers said a moratorium is not legal but deferring final votes within the 12-month window is. Nine applications reach their deadline before September 15, 2027. The same night, the Board denied the Tech Park at Dulles substation 6-3. [Loudoun Now](https://www.loudounnow.com/news/loudoun-supervisors-advance-12-month-pause-on-data-center-applications/article_33bdece6-af79-4b79-8bd0-169cf7b7181b.html); [United Loudoun](https://unitedloudoun.org/issues/pause); [WJLA](https://wjla.com/news/local/story/loudoun-county-data-centers-development-applications-board-supervisors-pause-northern-virginia-regulations-leesburg-catoctin-grid-reliability-dominion-energy-merger-power-lines-laws)
- Opposition: IBEW Local 26, the Loudoun Chamber of Commerce and the Data Center Coalition. Data centers bring in about $1.3B, roughly 40% of the FY2027 budget. [Loudoun Now](https://www.loudounnow.com/news/loudoun-supervisors-advance-12-month-pause-on-data-center-applications/article_33bdece6-af79-4b79-8bd0-169cf7b7181b.html)

### 4. Base rates
- I found no formal base rate for how often a Virginia county board adopts a resolution it has already directed staff to draft by a supermajority.
- Points that matter here:
  - The directive vote was 7-1-1, a large majority.
  - The item has been postponed once, and Randall described a first deferral as routine.
  - Deferrals requested by the County Attorney suggest unsettled legal questions.
  - From 2022 to May 2026 the Board approved 32 of 39 data center applications, so it has historically favored development.
- Similar local pauses have passed elsewhere. For example, Carroll County, Maryland, extended its data center deferral through February 2028. [Fox Baltimore](https://foxbaltimore.com/news/local/carroll-county-board-of-commissioners-extends-data-center-development-pause-through-2028-maryland)

### 5. Other forecasts
- I found no Polymarket, Kalshi or Manifold market on the Loudoun pause.
- The Kalshi markets collected for this report are related but do not match the question:
  - "Any state enacts a data center moratorium law": 0.29 before January 1, 2027, and 0.94 before 2028.
  - Loudoun Water data center water use, Q1 2027: above 250 million gallons at 0.48.

  These are only loose signals about the political climate.
- I could not see the Metaculus community forecast for question 46271.

### 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- About 2026-11-12: the agenda packet for November 17 should be posted on eScribe. Check whether item 14p is still listed and whether staff recommend adopting it.
- 2026-11-17: the scheduled Board business meeting and vote. Possible outcomes are adoption, adoption with the substation part removed, another deferral, or rejection. One point to judge carefully: if the Board removes substations, as Letourneau suggested, the question would not count it, because it requires a pause on both data centers and substations.
- Early December 2026: there may be another Board business meeting before December 16. I could not confirm the date. That leaves at most one more chance if the item is deferred again.
- December 2026: Dominion's Golden substation application was deferred to December. It could test the grid-reliability exception. [Loudoun Now](https://www.loudounnow.com/news/loudoun-supervisors-advance-12-month-pause-on-data-center-applications/article_33bdece6-af79-4b79-8bd0-169cf7b7181b.html)
- The County Attorney's further legal consultation and any legal threats from industry could lead to more delay.

forecasts.reasoning:
(a) There are about 39 days until the December 16, 2026 deadline. For Yes, the Loudoun Board of Supervisors must formally adopt a resolution or other official action that generally pauses its final votes on legislative applications for both data centers and electrical substations. Exceptions for grid reliability or statutory deadlines are allowed. The scheduled vote is November 17. December business meetings, likely around December 1 and/or December 15, would be fallback dates.

(b) If nothing changed, there would be no pause. As of November 7 nothing has been adopted, and the vote has already been deferred once, from October 20 to November 17.

(c) Base rate: when a local governing board votes by a clear supermajority (here 7-1-0-1) to have staff draft a specific resolution, that resolution is usually adopted in some form within a few months. I estimate roughly 75-85% eventually pass. A smaller share pass by a specific near-term date once deferrals are counted, perhaps 60-70% within two meetings of the scheduled date.

(d) Evidence:
- **For Yes:**
  - On September 15 the Board voted 7-1-0-1 to draft the resolution, and 7-1-0-1 again to approve the exceptions framework.
  - The same day it denied the Tech Park at Dulles substation 6-3.
  - October reporting says most supervisors back the pause, and Briskman is publicly pushing for the vote.
  - The draft already covers both data centers and substations, and its exceptions fit the fine print.
  - The Board wants the pause to apply retroactively to September 15, which shows commitment.
  - The November 17 vote is firmly scheduled, and at least one more meeting before December 16 is likely if it slips.
- **For No:**
  - Chair Randall postponed the vote twice, and the county attorney requested the October 20 deferral after letters from developer attorneys.
  - Industry opposes the pause (Data Center Coalition and Chamber of Commerce, October 5), and lawsuits are threatened.
  - About 40% of the county budget comes from the sector, which creates institutional caution.
  - The Board could also narrow the scope, for example dropping substations, or turn it into a non-binding policy.

(e) **No scenario:** On November 17, legal review prompts a further deferral or substantive rewrite. The revised version cannot be heard before mid-December, or the December calendar has only one meeting and it slips into January.
**Yes scenario:** On November 17 the 7-member majority adopts the pause, with grid-reliability and statutory-deadline exceptions, effective back to September 15.

(f) I start at about 70% for passage by a near-term date. The size of the majority, the firm scheduling, and the backup meetings push this up. The repeated deferrals, the chair's reluctance, and active legal pressure pull it down. On balance I land slightly above the base rate. No market covers this question.

Probability: 72%
